newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses higher, dollar at two-year peak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses higher, dollar at two-year peak.

text.p: European bourses ended the day with healthy gains on Wednesday and the dollar hit a two-year high against the mark as currency traders got the jitters over upcoming German jobless figures.

Stocks began the day with solid advances on the strength of another record close on Wall Street overnight. Wednesday's unsteady opening in New York failed to dent the positive performances on this side of the Atlantic.
The dollar hit its two-year peak of 1.5763 marks in late trading, more than a pfennig up on levels seen late on Tuesday,

"It's been helped this morning by rumours about Yeltsin's health and I think there's also some buying sparked by expectations of weak German unemployment data coming in tomorrow," said David Brown, chief European economist at Bear Stearns.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin spent Wednesday at his country residence outside Moscow nursing a heavy cold but the surgeon who gave him a multiple heart bypass two months ago said there was no cause for alarm.
German markets are often sensitive to concern about uncertainty in Russia in view of close economic and geographical ties between the two countries.
Nerves over the German December jobless data undermined the mark because poor figures could increase pressure for interest rate cuts, making the mark less attractive to investors.
"It (weaker German jobs data) could spark more rate cut speculation and that's going to build up ahead of the Bundesbank council meeting tomorrow," said Brown.
The German central bank's policy-making council is also due to hold its first regular meeting of the year on Thursday.
The dollar was also stronger against the yen, testing the 116 yen level. But traders said the rise was a correction after its recent decline against the Japanese currency.
London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, ended trading up 0.2 percent after losses on Tuesday. Business, however, was cautious because of interest rate anxiety and Wall Street's recent volatility.
"People are starting to worry that interest rates may be pushed up sooner rather than later," one senior dealer said.
Foreign-earning companies were hit by continuing concerns about the impact of a strong pound sterling on profits.
Other European bourses ended at higher levels but the mood was nervous because of worries that record-breaking levels of recent weeks could not be sustained much longer.

Nerves were not helped by a disappointing opening in New York after closing at a record level in the previous session. Wall Street ended up 33.48 points at 6,600.66 on Tuesday, surpassing Monday's peak of 6,567.18.
French stocks closed showing gains of 1.3 percent despite Wall Street's downturn. The dollar's strength gave the market a lift because of improved export prospects, traders said.
But brokers said the market was unlikely to make further big gains ahead of important U.S. economic indicators due out on Thursday and Friday.
In Frankfurt, stocks ended floor trade up 0.7 percent, boosted by the strengthening dollar and the positive debt market.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.5763 marks and 115.83 yen compared with 1.5634 and 115.25 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 8.7 points higher at 4,087.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 29.93 at 2,331.62.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 20.21 at 2,906.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold finished at $355.75, well below Tuesday's London close of $359.35. Silver ended at $4.66, down six cents.
